- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) or near-zero — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast if sentiment is weak or recently negative — model often overreacts.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, reduce next forecast by 1-2% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Lagged overreaction: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often holds high forecast for 2-3 days — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating early days (first 5–7) when sentiment is bullish — cap early forecast peaks at 1.5–2% below recent high.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, reduce forecast volatility — model tends to overfit recent noise.
